title: TrailGuard AI camera in Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary transmits images of armed poachers on two nights; Dudhwa Tiger Reserve officials identify them and investigate
summary: Dertien et al. (BioScience 2023): one TrailGuard AI unit captured poachers 'carrying a gun and knives' on two dates and a poached chital; officials identified them. Arrests claimed only in releases.
account: Dertien, Negi, Dinerstein and colleagues (BioScience 73(10):748-757, published online 14 September 2023, the date used here because the paper does not date the detections) report deploying the TrailGuard AI camera-alert system, which 'runs on-the-edge artificial intelligence algorithms to detect tigers and poachers and transmit real-time images', in the Kanha-Pench corridor and in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh. All seven Dudhwa units transmitted images; three transmitted objects of interest to forest department officials. 'One unit within Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary captured a group of poachers carrying a gun and knives on two separate dates, and a presumably poached chital (Axis axis) on the second detection'; 'Authorities were able to quickly identify the individuals via the transmitted images and were investigating the matter'. Tigers were detected at the same spot three days before the second poacher detection. The authors include RESOLVE and CVEDIA staff (the system's developers) alongside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum co-authors. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim of 'identifying a team of poachers'. A Clemson University release of 15 September 2023, which carries Nightjar/RESOLVE boilerplate, states that the alerts 'led the authorities to the arrest of these individuals for poaching a few weeks later' and quotes Sanjay Kumar Pathak, former field director of Dudhwa, that the system 'led to the detection and arrest of poachers in Dudhwa'; The Hindu (16 September 2023) reported, citing a person involved in the experiment, that poachers caught on camera had a year later helped forest authorities secure a conviction, and quoted Piyush Yadav of Nightjar, the manufacturer, that 'A year down, these poachers were arrested with images from TrailGuard playing a key role'; the article's lead places the capture in Kanha-Pench while the Yadav quote places it in Dudhwa. No forest-department statement or court record of an arrest was found. Existing record AIBD-0102 concerns TrailGuard AI at Similipal, Odisha.
purpose: Built to detect tigers and people on trails with embedded AI and send real-time images to forest officials; detecting and transmitting the poachers' images was that purpose.
system: TrailGuard AI camera-alert system (embedded AI on an Intel computer-vision chip; cellular transmission)
developer: Nightjar / RESOLVE, Washington DC (inventor Steve Gulick), with CVEDIA Ltd
deployer: Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh Forest Department, with the Global Tiger Forum, National Tiger Conservation Authority and Clemson University
location: Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary, Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh, India
taxonomy_note: Environmental sustainability because the protected asset is wildlife in a tiger reserve. 'Protective response' because the documented outcome is officials identifying and investigating the poachers from the transmitted images; an arrest, which would make it harm prevented, appears only in a university release quoting the former field director and in developer material, not in the peer-reviewed paper or any official record.

ratings.reason: Forest officials received the images in near real time and identified the individuals; the paper documents an investigation, not an arrest or prosecution, so the recorded gain is an investigative lead.

Protection of the reserve's wildlife from this gang is claimed through arrests only in the Clemson release, developer material and The Hindu's second-hand report; the paper notes a chital presumably poached before the second detection.

ai_role.statement: The camera's on-board classifier filtered motion triggers to people and tigers and transmitted the poachers' images to officials' phones within about a minute; identification and investigation were done by officials. The peer-reviewed account is co-authored by the developers (RESOLVE, CVEDIA) with Dudhwa and Wildlife Institute of India staff and stops at 'investigating'; the arrest claim rests on a Clemson release quoting the former field director, on developer press releases and on The Hindu quoting the manufacturer and an unnamed participant.

later.note: Two days after the paper, The Hindu quoted Nightjar's Piyush Yadav that the Dudhwa poachers were arrested about a year after the images, with TrailGuard images playing a key role; Clemson's release of 15 September 2023 says the arrests came a few weeks later, and no forest department or court record was found.
later.quote: But in the Dudhwa [tiger reserve] we learnt that not only could we track [in this case] tigers approaching a village but we also caught a gang of poachers on camera who were walking with a hunted chital. claim_basis: Three independent news reports, two peer-reviewed studies from the makers and the deployer's press release are on file. There is no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.
